title: 48th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with announcements, three requests to remove members of the Anti-Corruption, Civil Service and Elections Commissions (all sent to the Independent Institutions Committee), and the first reading of a resolution on Israeli passports. Opening debate on the 2025 state budget followed: opposition members criticised the lack of detail and the subsidy changes, while government-side members defended it as a housing, health and deficit-cutting budget. After a break the Majlis passed the Tobacco Control Act amendment bill 54 to 0, with 8 abstentions.

Debate on the 2025 state budget
items.outcome: debated; opening speeches, to resume the next day at 10:30

items.title: Committee report on the Tobacco Control Act (2010/15) amendment bill

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the budget lacks the usual itemised detail and breaks the law on block grants to councils.
Argued loan disbursements should count as spending, so the deficit cut is overstated, and questioned subsidy cuts without a targeting plan.
Questioned the PSIP spending figures and the rise in staff and political appointee costs.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the budget as properly prepared, praising health spending on cancer care and bone marrow transplants.
Argued card subsidies currently reach wealthy people and foreign workers, and that direct payments to accounts are fairer.
Highlighted MVR 1.5 billion for housing and expanded youth education loans.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Thanked the finance minister and backed the budget as one that lowers the deficit compared with earlier years.
Welcomed housing, health and land allocations, including support for Kaashidhoo plots.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Described the budget as a housing, health and social protection budget with a MVR 12.5 billion fiscal reform.
Pointed to planned hospitals, Aasandha strengthening, housing projects and student loans.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the budget, noting the deficit falls to MVR 9.4 billion from 13.6 billion last year.
Listed Addu City items: the Hulhudhoo-Hithadhoo bridge, roads, power outages, a new Feydhoo school and housing.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Called the budget realistic and well studied compared with earlier ones, naming health, housing and land reclamation.
Said direct subsidies are meant to reach those in need and that Aasandha and ENSPA will not be cut.
Accused MDP members of misleading the public on subsidies.

speakers.name: Asma Rasheed
positions: Presented the Social Committee report on the Tobacco Control Act amendment bill.
Explained two changes: smoking banned on state office grounds per regulations, and approved cessation therapies not treated as tobacco.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Said he backs controlling and banning vapes and tobacco imports but called the bill poorly prepared.
Said stakeholders and councils were not properly consulted and police said it cannot be enforced.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said he shares concerns about the committee process and enforceability, and about traders who hold permits.
Criticised rushed decisions at the president's request and said he would not vote.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said the committee heard stakeholders and made substantial changes to the original bill.
Pointed to the exemption allowing designated smoking areas and the carve-out for nicotine replacement therapy.

decisions: Three removal requests (Anti-Corruption, Civil Service and Elections Commissions) were sent to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The Speaker announced the 2025 budget debate would continue at 10:30 the next day, with 15 minutes per member.
A committee-of-the-whole meeting on the Political Parties Act amendment bill was announced for later in the day.
The Tobacco Control Act (2010/15) amendment bill passed 54-0 with 8 abstentions.
The next sitting was set for 13 November 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Passing the Tobacco Control Act (2010/15) amendment bill as reported by the committee
